answer: Capped standing-intake resists sybils: the system grants new establishment to at most a fixed number of identities per epoch through a slow admission queue, so a sudden flood cannot all reach the summit of influence at once. A hollow swarm registered together just serializes behind the valve, stretching the attacker's wall-clock time to K divided by the intake rate — many epochs of patient juniper-slow waiting — while an honest trickle passes unaffected. Influence cannot be acquired in bulk instantly; the global rate cap turns a one-shot flood into a long, costly drip.
